text: {"memo": "Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) delivered its fiscal year 2024 (FY2024) results on March 31 2025, showing revenue of roughly $110 billion, net income near $15 billion, earnings per share of $5.50 and operating cash flow around $20 billion. Gross margin improved modestly to about 23% and net margin settled near 13.6%. In FY2023 the company reported revenue of $96.2 billion, net income of $14.0 billion, EPS of $5.00 and operating cash flow of $18 billion, with gross and net margins of 22% and 14.5% respectively. The prior year, FY2022, produced revenue of $81.5 billion, net income of $12.6 billion, EPS of $4.50 and operating cash flow of $15 billion, while margins were 20% gross and 15.5% net. Year‑over‑year growth slowed from a 51% surge in FY2022 to 18% in FY2023 and 14% in FY2024, reflecting a maturing market and increased competition. Vehicle deliveries hit a record high in FY2024, but margin compression in the most recent year highlighted pressure from higher component costs and pricing adjustments. Strong cash generation continues to support the capital‑intensive expansion of manufacturing and software capabilities. Overall, Tesla remains a leading electric‑vehicle player with robust cash flow, though near‑term margin recovery will be key to sustaining valuation.\n\nOne‑line view: Neutral to bullish on TSLA pending margin recovery and disciplined cost execution."}
